question: _______ unemployment refers to the lowest unemployment level a healthy economy can sustain without causing inflation.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Natural unemployment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natural unemployment:-**

 
 
• It is also known as the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment (NAIRU).
 
• It is the level of unemployment below which inflation starts to rise due to increasing labor costs.
 
• The natural rate of unemployment is determined by structural factors such as changes in technology, demographics, and globalization, and is beyond the control of monetary policy.
 
• The natural rate of unemployment can vary over time and across countries due to differences in labor market institutions, regulations, and social norms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Structural unemployment:-**

 
 
• It refers to the mismatch between the skills and qualifications of workers and the requirements of available jobs. 
 
• It can occur due to changes in the economy, such as technological advancements or shifts in consumer preferences.
 
 
 
• **Disguised unemployment:-**
 
 
• It refers to a situation where workers are employed but their contribution to production is negligible or redundant.
 
• It can occur in sectors with low productivity or in economies with a large informal sector.
 
 
 
• **Frictional unemployment:-**
 
 
• It refers to the temporary unemployment that occurs when workers are searching for better job opportunities or transitioning between jobs. 
 
• It can be reduced by improving labor market information and reducing search costs for job seekers.
